{{Short description|Type of path on Platonic solids}}
{{Technical|date=June 2026}}
A '''Yellow brick road''' is "the unique simple closed path that solves the antisocial jogger problem for any of the [[Platonic solids]]. Such a path must (1) begin and end at a single vertex of the solid, and (2) be a straight line path that may cross over edges, but may not pass through any other vertices."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4670422|title=Yellow Brick Road Path on Regular Dodecahedron by MathMaker|website=Thingiverse - The community for Open Hardware}}</ref> The solution for the [[dodecahedron]] was given by mathematicians [[Jayadev Athreya]] and David Aulicino in a paper published 11 February 2019,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00029890.2019.1538475|title=A Trajectory from a Vertex to Itself on the Dodecahedron|first1=Jayadev S.|last1=Athreya|first2=David|last2=Aulicino|date=February 7, 2019|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=126|issue=2|pages=161–162|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/00029890.2019.1538475|arxiv=1802.00811}}</ref> and its area division was given by [[Li Zhou]] in a paper published 11 October 2021.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhou |first=Li |date=2021-11-26 |title=Area Division of the Yellow Brick Road on the Regular Dodecahedron |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00029890.2021.1977886 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |language=en |volume=128 |issue=10 |pages=897–897 |doi=10.1080/00029890.2021.1977886 |issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{Portal|Mathematics}}
